info.title: Single server, general service times (M/G/1)
info.description: The single-server queue with Poisson arrivals (one a minute) and a service time that is not exponential: uniform between 0.2 and 1.4 minutes, mean 0.8. The server is as busy as in an M/M/1 queue of the same load (80%), but the queue is shorter, because the service time varies less. Read the Server's average queue length: the Pollaczek-Khinchine formula gives lambda^2 E[S^2] / (2 (1 - rho)) = 0.76 / 0.4 = 1.9.
info.notes: E[S] = 0.8 and Var[S] = 1.2^2 / 12 = 0.12, so E[S^2] = 0.76 and rho = 0.8. With an exponential service time of the same mean the queue would hold 3.2 on average. A short run scatters widely around 1.9; lengthen the run or add replications to see it settle.
